title: Alex Attard Graded Repertoire · Level 1 · Baroque & Classical

practice.haydn-surprise-theme: Light, short eighth notes over a steady left hand. Keep everything soft, so the last chord really is a surprise.
practice.beethoven-ode-to-joy: A melody that moves by step: keep it smooth and connected. Loop bars 9 to 12, then hold the tied note across into bar 13.
practice.mozart-theme-k265: Even quarter notes in both hands. The left hand moves while the right hand repeats, so learn the left hand alone first.
practice.handel-conquering-hero: Long notes that sing, and eighth-note runs that stay even. Loop bars 13 to 16, where the C sharps are.
practice.haydn-emperor-hymn: It starts halfway through the bar: count 1, 2 and come in on 3. Loop bars 15 and 16 until the quick notes are even.
practice.mozart-minuet-k2: Your first minuet: three beats in a bar, with a strong first beat. Play each hand alone before putting them together.
practice.petzold-minuet-in-g: Eighth notes that run evenly into a quarter note. Loop bars 1 and 2, then find every pair of bars like them.
practice.petzold-minuet-in-g-minor: The partner of the Minuet in G, now in a minor key. Name the two flats before you play, and watch for accidentals.
practice.minuet-in-c-minor-anh121: Three flats in the key signature: name them before you start. Learn it four bars at a time.
practice.musette-in-d-anh126: The left hand jumps an octave, like a bagpipe drone. Practise the left-hand jumps alone until you can play them without looking.
practice.minuet-in-g-anh116: The longest piece in the book. Learn it in four-bar sections, looping each one before moving on.
practice.march-in-e-flat-anh127: The hardest piece in the book: triplets over steady quarter notes. Clap the triplets with the metronome before you play them.
